name: Chalcolepidius lenzi
intro: In August 2021 I kept a female alongside a separately housed female of Chalcolepidius smaragdinus.

facts.title: Container
facts.text: One US gallon (3.8 L), well ventilated

facts.title: Floor
facts.text: 1.3 in (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber with bark flats

sections.title: Adults
sections.text:
I used a ventilated one-gallon tub (3.8 L) with about 1.3 inches (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber. Flat pieces of bark gave the female cover and a surface she could grip to right herself. I did not record eggs or offspring. In Chalcolepidius webbi, Alan found eggs on bark and paper towel, both surfaces I would check in a future trial.
Females have serrate antennae. The teeth are more pronounced in males (Casari, 2002).

sources.title: My two adult housing trials, August 2021
